messages:
user_jordan: Hey team — after upgrading my app and running `poetry install` I can no longer import the SDK. I did `from redwood import RedwoodClient` and get ImportError. Was working yesterday. Python 3.11, poetry 1.4.0, pip 23.2

alex-support: sorry about that — can you paste the exact traceback and the output of `python -c 'import redwood; print(redwood.__file__); print(redwood.__version__)'` and `poetry show --tree`? Also which package name did you install (redwood vs redwood-sdk)?

user_jordan: Traceback:```Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
ImportError: cannot import name 'RedwoodClient' from 'redwood' (/home/jordan/project/redwood/__init__.py)
```I did `poetry add redwood-sdk` per the quickstart. `poetry show --tree` shows `redwood-sdk 0.8.2` -> `redwood 0.8.2` etc.

sam: two quick checks: `python -c 'import sys; print(sys.path)'` and `ls -la` in your project root. The traceback path points to /home/jordan/project/redwood/__init__.py which smells like a local folder named redwood shadowing the package.

user_jordan: ahhh. I do have a `redwood/` dir in my repo for demo scripts. Didn't think that would matter. Output:```/home/jordan/.local/share/pypoetry/venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py
0.8.2
```But the traceback earlier pointed to `/home/jordan/project/redwood/__init__.py` when I ran from my project root.

alex-support: yep that's the culprit 99% of the time. When you run from project root, Python will first look for a top-level package folder named `redwood` in CWD and import that. Rename your local folder or run from a different CWD. Quick workaround: `python -c "import sys; sys.path.remove('') ; import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"` (this forces ignoring cwd).

user_jordan: tried renaming the folder to `rd_demo` then `python -c 'from redwood import RedwoodClient; print("ok")'` — now works. Thanks!

maya: filing a note for docs — we'll add a section about local package name collisions in the Python quickstart (good catch). @alex-support can you capture the repro steps?

alex-support: filed internal ticket #INC-1429 and added repro: create top-level folder `redwood/` with `__init__.py`, run script from repo root, import resolves to local module not installed package.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-1429 — python quickstart doc update requested.

sam: followup: if folks see similar import errors but no local dir, ask to run `pip show redwood` and `python -c 'import inspect, redwood; print(inspect.getsource(redwood))'` to confirm which module is loading. Also if using editable installs (`pip install -e .`) ensure package name in setup/pyproject doesn't conflict with a module you also have in repo.

user_jordan: reinstalled with `poetry run pip install --force-reinstall redwood-sdk==0.8.2` just to be safe and all good now. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
